Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really useful conversation on the use case and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap:
- Use case: ingest meeting transcripts + shared docs (20k-120k tokens) to power executive summaries and question-answering for product and GTM teams.
- Key constraints: high fidelity summarization, predictable truncation behavior (must not drop final decisions), and budget target ~ $0.002 / 1k tokens after optimizations.
- Security: data residency in US, SOC 2 required (we covered evidence checklist).

Recommended evaluation plan (what we’ll deliver in a short pilot):
1) Long-context model fit matrix: run 3 candidate models across your sample dataset (baseline open-llama-70b, optimized LLM-A-30b, and Redwood Long-Context v1) measuring summarization fidelity, hallucination rate, and truncation/rollover behavior.
2) Prompt sets: we’ll run the canonical summarization and Q&A prompt sets you shared plus aggressive-context-window prompts (we’ve attached the initial prompt sets).
3) Benchmarks and artifacts: we’ll return per-document csv with token breakdowns, latency, and quality scores; initial results targeted in 48–72 hours.

Attachments: prompt-sets.zip (initial prompt templates), MAP-Acme-20260310.pdf (mutual action plan), acme_long_context_eval_results.csv (placeholder for results).

Next steps:
- I’ll kick off the eval run with Neha (SE) today — expect preliminary results by Thu morning PT.
- Rishi will loop in pricing options for Dedicated vs Hosted with cost breakdowns after we have per-token estimates.
- Alex / Priya: can you confirm the final sample corpus (we discussed ~150 transcripts + 200 supporting docs) and the data sharing method (SFTP or shared Drive)?

If that looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for a quick results review Thurs 9am PT.

Alex — thanks, adding technical detail below. I’m starting the eval run this morning and will post results to the Drive link once the jobs finish. High-level plan and notes: 

Truncation / preservation strategies we’ll evaluate:
- Sliding-window with overlapping summaries (stride tuned to preserve last N tokens) — good for extracting decisions from the tail.
- KV-cache stitching on Redwood Long-Context v1 (keeps state across segments) — expected to preserve coherence and avoid repeat generation.
- Prefix-preservation: prepend a short "closing-summary" extractor segment to force the model to attend to end-of-document content.

Model candidates (we’ll run identical prompts across these):
- open-llama-70b (baseline) — full fp16 run for quality baseline.
- LLM-A-30b (optimized) — 4-bit quantized run to measure perf/cost tradeoffs.
- Redwood Long-Context v1 — our extended-kv model optimized for >200k tokens (experimental rollout).

Metrics and artifacts:
- Automatic: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, factuality score (QA-based), action-item recall (custom script that checks if annotated action items appear in the summary), token counts, latency.
- Human eval: we’ll surface 30 gold summaries for blind annotation (you provide), and we’ll report Precision/Recall on action items.
- Regression checks: We’ll run baseline regression tests vs your historical golds and flag any degradation >5% on action-item recall.

Quantization notes:
- 4-bit quantization on LLM-A-30b reduces cost ~40–55% but can increase hallucination risk; we’ll report differences per metric.
- For summary fidelity, our recommendation is to prefer fp16 for final pass; quantized runs are useful for cost-bound tiers and fast iteration.

Benchmarks / links:
- Long-context benchmark writeup: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/long-context-summary-2026
- Drive folder with eval artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-long-context-evals
- Prompt sets (we used): attached prompt-sets.zip

I’ll upload acme_long_context_eval_results.csv (raw per-doc results) and a short executive summary to the Drive once the runs complete. Marissa — I set the preliminary review for Thu 9am PT; if that still works I’ll send the invite.

-Neha
